ray-ds and raylang

ray-ds is framework-agnostic: the components are standard custom elements with no dependencies, and they work in any page, in React, in Vue, in a browser or in any webview. Nothing in a component requires raylang.

raylang is where ray-ds comes from and where it gets extras. This page says what those extras are today and the plan for the ones that make a raylang app better than any other host: a bridge to the native side, and a raylang package that brings the whole design system without npm.

Today

  • Tooling in raylang. Tokens, contrast checks, docs, the npm packages and the browser tests are generated and run by tools/ (ray run tools/src/main.ray build).
  • Made for the std/ui webview. No build step: the elements load as ES modules from ray://app, and form fields are form-associated, so a FormData reaches the program through window.ray.send or window.ray.request as it is.
  • Examples. examples/desktop-form (plain HTML), examples/react-app and examples/vue-app (made with ray new --frontend react-ts|vue-ts) drive the page in the real webview and check what reaches raylang.
  • The native bridge (plan 1, milestones 1 to 4): system file dialogs with real paths (ray-file-upload native, ray-path-input), native confirmations (confirmDialog()), native context menus (ray-menu native), the app's menu bar in the command palette (native-menus), and the window: ray-app-shell under a transparent title bar, window colors that follow the theme, and the "unsaved changes" mark (trackEdits). See below.

Using the bridge

In the program, answer the bridge before the app's own events (ray_ds = "path:…/ray-ds/ray_ds" in [dependencies] until the package is published):

import std/ui;
import ray_ds/bridge;

for e in ui.events() {
    if (bridge.handle(e)) {
        continue;   // a ray-ds request, already answered
    }
    // the app's own events
}

In the page, once:

import { enableRaylang } from "ray-ds/core/raylang.js";   // or from "@ray-ds/elements"
await enableRaylang();   // the host, or null in a browser
<ray-file-upload native multiple accept=".png,.jpg" label="Photos"></ray-file-upload>
<ray-path-input name="out" label="Export to" mode="save" accept=".csv"></ray-path-input>

ray-file-upload native lists the chosen files as HostFiles (name, size, type and path), gives their paths in paths and submits the paths with its form; drop and paste still give Files. ray-path-input shows Browse… only with the host. confirmDialog() asks with the system dialog unless native: false. In a browser all of them behave as before.

For menus, keep one Native for the whole loop, declare the menus through it and use route(), which turns an item run from the palette into the same "menu" event the menu bar sends:

let n = bridge.system();
bridge.menu(n, "File", [ui.item("new", "New", "cmd+n"), ui.item("open", "Open…", "cmd+o")])?;
for raw in ui.events() {
    let e = match (bridge.route(n, raw)) {
        Option.Some(e) => e,      // for the app
        Option.None => continue,  // answered by the bridge
    };
    if (e.kind == "menu") { … }   // from the menu bar or from the palette
}
<ray-command-palette native-menus></ray-command-palette>
<ray-menu native context>
  <div slot="trigger">…</div>
  <ray-menu-item value="rename">Rename</ray-menu-item>
</ray-menu>

bridge.menu_at, replace_menu and set_menu_item keep the record up to date the same way (bridge.record records a menu without touching the bar).

The window: open it with o.kind = "full_content" and enableRaylang() sets --ray-titlebar-height and --ray-titlebar-inset (the room for the macOS window buttons) on <html>; a ray-app-shell then makes its header the title bar (taller, indented, dragging the window) or, with layout="alt" or no header, starts its navbar and main below it. dragRegion(el) does the same for any element of your own. enableRaylang() also keeps the window's background and title bar in the theme's background color (windowColors: false to opt out), and trackEdits(form) marks the window as edited while the form differs from what was saved:

import { enableRaylang, trackEdits } from "@ray-ds/elements";
await enableRaylang();
const edits = trackEdits(document.querySelector("form"));   // edits.dirty, edits.clean()

Principles

  • The components stay agnostic. No component imports the bridge. Without it, every component behaves exactly as it does today, in any host.
  • Opt-in and detectable. The bridge is one module, enabled by the app, and only active when window.ray exists. A page shared between a browser and a std/ui window works in both.
  • One source of truth. The package, its assets and its types are generated by the same build that writes the npm packages, from the same component.toml files.

Plan 1: the native bridge

A small protocol between the page and the program, with two halves:

  • Page: core/raylang.js (in @ray-ds/elements, also re-exported from its index). enableRaylang() detects window.ray, asks the program for its capabilities once ("hello") and installs a host in core/host.js, the registry the components ask; they never import the bridge.
  • Program: a raylang module, ray_ds/bridge (the ray_ds/ directory of this repo), with one entry point for the app's event loop:
import std/ui;
import ray_ds/bridge;

for e in ui.events() {
    if (bridge.handle(e)) {
        continue;   // a ray-ds request, already answered
    }
    // the app's own events
}

Requests travel through window.ray.request as JSON ({"ray-ds": 1, "op": "pick_files", …}) and bridge.handle answers them with ui.reply_json: {"ok": true, "value": …} or {"ok": false, "error": "…"}. Anything else passes through untouched, so the bridge coexists with the app's own protocol. The dialogs sit behind a Native struct (bridge.system()); handle_with(e, n) takes another one, which is how the webview tests answer with scripted dialogs.

Operation Asks for Answers
hello {protocol, version, platform, ops}
pick_files title, directory, multiple, filters [{path, name, size}], [] if cancelled
pick_path mode (open, folder, save), title, directory, suggested, filters the path, or null
confirm title, message, confirmLabel, cancelLabel, style true / false
menu_items [{menu, tag, title, shortcut, enabled, checked}] (no separators, no role:*)
run_menu tag true; route() gives the app the "menu" event
popup_menu id, items (title, enabled, checked, separator) true once shown; the choice comes later as the page event ray-ds:menu ({id, index}), nothing when dismissed
window_colors background, titlebar (#rrggbb, "" = system) true
set_edited edited true

What the components get

Component With the bridge raylang API
ray-file-upload "browse" opens the native dialog with filters built from accept and returns real paths (paths property, read on change); drop and paste keep working with File objects ui.pick_files, ui.file_options, ui.filter
ray-path-input (new) a field with a "Browse…" button for a file, a folder or a save target, showing the chosen path; without the bridge it is a plain text field ui.pick_file_with, ui.pick_folder_with, ui.save_file_with
ray-command-palette lists the app's native menu items next to its own commands, with their shortcuts; running one emits the same menu event as the menu ui.menu (recorded through bridge.menu)
ray-menu native attribute: opens as a native context menu at the pointer; the choice arrives as ray-select ui.popup_menu
confirmDialog() asks with the native, modal dialog instead of a ray-dialog ui.confirm, ui.message_styled
ray-sidebar, app header in a full_content window, reserve window.ray.titlebar_height and mark the header as the drag handle (data-ray-drag), so the page runs under a transparent macOS title bar window kind full_content
Theme when the user picks light, dark or a primary color, the window background and title bar follow, so a resize or reopen never flashes the other theme ui.set_background, ui.set_titlebar_color
Forms optional edited tracking: a dirty form marks the window as edited (the macOS dot) ui.set_edited
Attachments "open" and "show in folder" for an attachment with a path ui.open_path, ui.reveal

Milestones

  1. ✅ Protocol and loop. core/raylang.js and ray_ds/bridge with capability negotiation, pick_files and confirm. Tests: the raylang tests of bridge.answer, and tests/bridge.test.js, where the page talks to the real bridge in the webview runner (scripted dialogs).
  2. ✅ Files. ray-file-upload native and the new ray-path-input (pick_path), with their React/Vue wrappers and types.
  3. ✅ Menus. bridge.menu (and menu_at, replace_menu, set_menu_item), route(), the palette listing native items (native-menus), ray-menu native.
  4. ✅ Window. full_content support in ray-app-shell (header as the title bar, dragRegion), theme to window colors, trackEdits. The drag handle works around finding #138 (the shell's data-ray-drag does not see shadow DOM).
  5. Docs and example. A "raylang" section in each affected component's docs and an examples/desktop-app that uses all of it, driven by --check like the other examples.

Each milestone ships on its own and keeps the components working without the bridge.

Plan 2: the raylang package

A Tier-2 package, ray-ds, so a raylang app gets the design system with ray add ray-ds, with no npm, no Node and no copied files.

import std/ui;
import ray_ds;

fn main() -> int {
    ray_ds.mount("ray-ds")?;      // serves ray://app/ray-ds/… from the binary
    let h = ui.open("App", "ray://app/index.html", 960, 640)?;
    …
}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="ray-ds/tokens.css">
<script type="module" src="ray-ds/index.js"></script>

Contents

  • ray_ds.mount(prefix): mounts the elements, tokens.css, base.css and raylang.js in the app's ray://app tree.
  • ray_ds/bridge (plan 1).
  • The package is the ray_ds/ directory of this repo (it exists since plan 1 with bridge.ray); build adds the generated modules to it, the way it writes src/index.js. Its version is the version in ray-ds.toml.
  • The directory is ray_ds, not ray-ds: a path dependency is imported by the name of its directory, whatever its key in [dependencies] (finding #135). What name a git+ or index dependency gets is part of the spike.

How the assets travel

The package must work in ray run, in a native build and in a bundle, where the app runs with cwd=/ and only embedded assets exist. Two routes, to be decided by a spike:

  1. The package embeds them ([native] embed in the package's own ray.toml, mounted with ui.mount_embed_at). The raylang docs do not say whether a dependency's embed reaches the app's binary. If it does not, that goes to RAYLANG-FINDINGS.md.
  2. Generated module. build writes the assets as constants of a raylang module and mount serves them with ui.mount_bytes. It works with what the docs describe today; the spike measures the compile time and binary size.

Starting a project

ray new --frontend takes npm create vite templates, so it cannot start a ray-ds app without npm. Until raylang offers templates from a repository (another candidate finding), the package docs start from a minimal app (ray.toml, src/main.ray, assets/index.html) that is also kept as examples/starter and tested by the build.

Milestones

  1. Spike on the two asset routes; pick one.
  2. Package in packages/raylang/, generated by build, with mount and a raylang test that serves every file.
  3. Starter example and its --check.
  4. Publish in the index (github.com/ray-language/ray-index) and document ray add ray-ds in the README.

Later ideas

  • Typed HTML from raylang. From the same component.toml, generate a raylang module for compiled .ray.html templates with typed attributes (variant as an enum), so a misspelled variant fails at compile time. Since raylang 1.27.39 the compiled templates are documented and report clear errors (findings #126, #127 and #131 are resolved), so this no longer waits on raylang; it is the next candidate after plans 1 and 2.
  • Tokens in raylang. A generated tokens.ray, so charts drawn by the program, icons, the Info.plist colors or a native shell use the same palette as the UI.
  • UI tests for apps. The webview harness of tools/ as a utility: an app that uses ray-ds drives its own pages in the real webview from ray test.
  • System notifications. ray-notification could fall back to an OS notification when the window is not focused, but std/ui has no notification API today.
